name: Lake Chad
summary: Shallow endorheic lake shared with Chad, Niger, and Cameroon; open water has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.
description: Lake Chad once covered more than 25,000 km². Open water is now a fraction of that, replaced by marshes and receding shorelines. Nigeria's shoreline lies mainly in Borno and Yobe. The lake still supports fishing, recession agriculture, and transhumant pastoralism, and remains a focus of the Lake Chad Basin Commission.
areaNote: ~1,350 km² open water (highly variable; far below 1960s extent)
usage: Fishing, pastoralism, flood-recession farming, cross-border trade.
ecology: Wetland birds, seasonal inundation, desertification pressure, invasive typha in some channels.
climate: Sahel; rainfall decline and irrigation upstream affect inflows (Chari–Logone dominate).
significance: UNESCO concern over shrinkage; security and livelihood hotspot of the basin.
highlights: Livelihoods for millions in the basin

name: Kainji Lake
summary: Nigeria's largest man-made lake, impounded by Kainji Dam (1968).
description: Kainji Dam was a flagship independent-era hydropower project. The lake drowned settlements and created a major fishery and Kainji Lake National Park on adjoining shores. Water level and generation vary with Niger River flow and plant maintenance cycles.
maxDepthNote: ~12 m average; deeper near dam wall
usage: Hydroelectric power, fishing, limited navigation, tourism (national park).
ecology: Reservoir fishery; drawdown agriculture; wildlife in Kainji Lake National Park.
significance: First large Nigerian hydro dam; anchor of Niger State's Power State identity.

name: Lagos Lagoon
summary: Barrier-island lagoon behind Lagos; linked to the Atlantic through creeks and the harbour.
description: The lagoon is the water body that made Lagos a port city. It receives Ogun and Osun drainage, urban wastewater, and sand-mining pressure. Water transport (Lagos Waterways) and fishing remain active despite pollution and siltation.
maxDepthNote: ~2–5 m in main channels; shallower in flats
usage: Fishing, sand mining, urban drainage, ferry transport, port access.
ecology: Brackish water, mangroves (degraded), urban pollution hotspots.
significance: Historic harbour of Eko; Lekki–Lagos urban waterfront.

name: Oguta Lake
summary: Imo State's largest natural lake; a tourism and fishing landmark in the southeast.
description: Oguta Lake is a palm-fringed natural lake fed by the Njaba and Utu rivers. It hosts the Oguta Lake Holiday Complex, boat regattas, and lakeside settlements. Oil-palm processing and fishing sustain local communities.
usage: Tourism, fishing, boat transport, cultural festivals.
ecology: Freshwater fish species, riparian vegetation, linked wetland channels.
significance: Major natural lake of the Niger Delta hinterland; Imo tourism icon.

name: Goronyo Reservoir
summary: Large Sokoto basin reservoir supplying irrigation and downstream communities.
description: Goronyo Dam impounds the Rima River to provide dry-season irrigation for the Sokoto–Rima basin and water for Sokoto city. Siltation and variable rainfall affect storage capacity.
ecology: Seasonal drawdown exposes mudflats; bird habitat in wet season.
significance: Key water-security asset for northwest Nigeria.

name: Dadin Kowa Reservoir
summary: Gombe State reservoir on the Gongola, supporting hydropower and irrigation.
description: Dadin Kowa Dam regulates the Gongola River for the Dadin Kowa hydro plant and downstream irrigation in the Upper Benue basin. The reservoir also supports fishing and livestock watering.
significance: Major Gongola basin water infrastructure in the northeast.

name: Asejire Reservoir
summary: Oyo State reservoir on the Oshun River, supplying Ibadan and surrounding farms.
description: Asejire Dam was built in the late 1960s to provide water for Ibadan and irrigation in the Oshun valley. The lake is a weekend recreation spot and supports a local fishery.
usage: Domestic water for Ibadan, irrigation, fishing, recreation.
significance: Primary water source for Nigeria's third-largest city.

name: Challawa Gorge Reservoir
summary: Kano basin reservoir feeding irrigation and the Challawa hydro plant.
description: Challawa Gorge Dam impounds the Challawa River tributary of the Hadejia–Jama'are system. It supports Kano's hinterland irrigation schemes and the Challawa Gorge hydroelectric station.
significance: Part of the Hadejia–Jama'are basin water infrastructure.

name: Kainji Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: Nigeria's first major hydro plant (760 MW), on the Niger at Kainji Dam.
description: Commissioned in 1968, Kainji was the centrepiece of post-independence power expansion. Twelve turbine units draw from Kainji Lake. Output fluctuates with river flow and rehabilitation works.

name: Jebba Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 578 MW plant on the Niger downstream of Kainji, between Niger and Kwara states.
description: Jebba Dam regulates Niger flow for a 578 MW station operated downstream of Kainji. It is a key link in the Niger cascade and supports grid stability in central Nigeria.

name: Shiroro Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 600 MW plant on the Kaduna River in Niger State.
description: Shiroro Dam impounds the Kaduna River gorge northeast of Minna. The 600 MW plant is among Nigeria's most reliable hydro assets and supports the northern grid.

name: Zungeru Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 700 MW plant on the Kaduna River — Nigeria's newest major hydro asset.
description: Zungeru Dam was completed in the 2020s with Chinese financing. At 700 MW it is among the largest single hydro installations in Nigeria and strengthens supply to the national grid.

name: Dadin Kowa Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 40 MW plant on the Gongola River in Gombe State.
description: Dadin Kowa hydro uses the Dadin Kowa reservoir to generate power for the northeast grid while supplying irrigation water downstream.

name: Goronyo Dam Power & Irrigation
summary: Sokoto basin dam primarily for irrigation and water supply.
description: Goronyo Dam regulates the Rima River for dry-season farming in Sokoto State. While primarily an irrigation asset, it is listed among Nigeria's major water-control structures.
operator: Sokoto Rima River Basin Development Authority

name: Challawa Gorge Hydroelectric Station
summary: 39 MW plant on the Challawa River in Kano State.
description: Challawa Gorge Dam supports Kano basin irrigation and runs a 39 MW hydro station. It is part of the broader Hadejia–Jama'are water management system.

name: Tiga Hydroelectric Power Station
summary: 20 MW plant on the Hadejia River in Kano State.
description: Tiga Dam was built in the 1970s for irrigation and includes a 20 MW hydro station. It is upstream of Challawa in the Hadejia–Jama'are basin.

name: Ikere Gorge Hydroelectric Station
summary: 60 MW plant on the Ogun River in Oyo State.
description: Ikere Gorge Dam impounds the Ogun River for power generation and downstream flow regulation. It complements Asejire further upstream on the Oshun/Ogun system.

name: Obudu Dam Hydroelectric Station
summary: 70 MW plant in Cross River State supporting the southeast grid.
description: Obudu Dam on the Cross River system provides peaking power and supports tourism in the Obudu Plateau area. It is among the smaller but strategically placed hydro assets in the south.

name: Bakolori Dam
summary: Controversial Sokoto irrigation dam on the Sokoto River.
description: Bakolori Dam was built for irrigated wheat and rice schemes in Sokoto State. It became notable for downstream community displacement and water-access disputes, and is studied in Nigerian environmental history.
operator: Sokoto Rima River Basin Development Authority

name: Asejire Dam
summary: Multipurpose dam supplying Ibadan; linked to Asejire reservoir.
description: Asejire Dam primarily provides raw water for Ibadan and irrigation in the Oshun valley. It is a key urban water asset for southwestern Nigeria.

name: Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC)
summary: DISCO for the Federal Capital Territory and adjoining north-central states.
description: AEDC distributes grid power across the FCT and Niger, Kogi, and Nasarawa states from its Abuja headquarters, serving residential, government, and industrial load centres on the Abuja–Lokoja–Minna corridor.

name: Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC)
summary: South-south and southwest DISCO covering Edo, Delta, Ekiti, and Ondo.
description: BEDC operates from Benin City, distributing electricity across the Niger Delta fringe and the Edo–Ekiti–Ondo axis, including major cities such as Benin, Warri, Asaba, Akure, and Ado-Ekiti.

name: Eko Electricity Distribution Company (EKEDC)
summary: Lagos Island and south-eastern Lagos franchise DISCO.
description: EKEDC serves the Lagos Island, Apapa, Lekki, and Victoria Island axis from its Lagos headquarters, covering high-density commercial and residential load in Nigeria's economic capital.

name: Enugu Electricity Distribution Company (EEDC)
summary: Southeast DISCO for the five Igbo heartland states.
description: EEDC distributes power across Enugu, Abia, Imo, Anambra, and Ebonyi from Enugu, anchoring the eastern grid's urban and industrial consumers.

name: Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC)
summary: Southwest DISCO covering Oyo, Ogun, Osun, Kwara, and parts of Niger and Kogi.
description: IBEDC is one of Nigeria's largest DISCOs by customer count, operating from Ibadan across the southwest industrial belt and into Kwara and the Niger–Kogi fringe.

name: Ikeja Electric (IE)
summary: Mainland and northern Lagos franchise DISCO.
description: Ikeja Electric serves mainland Lagos, Ikeja, Oshodi, and the northern Lagos industrial corridors from its Ikeja headquarters, complementing EKEDC's island franchise.

name: Jos Electricity Distribution Company (JED)
summary: North-central DISCO for Plateau, Bauchi, Benue, and Gombe.
description: JED distributes electricity from Jos across the Plateau highlands and into Bauchi, Benue, and Gombe, serving mining towns, universities, and farming communities.

name: Kaduna Electricity Distribution Company (KAEDCO)
summary: Northwest DISCO for Kaduna, Sokoto, Kebbi, and Zamfara.
description: KAEDCO operates from Kaduna city, distributing power across the northwestern savanna states with major load centres in Kaduna, Zaria, Sokoto, and Gusau.

name: Kano Electricity Distribution Company (KEDCO)
summary: Northwest DISCO for Kano, Jigawa, and Katsina.
description: KEDCO distributes electricity from Kano across Nigeria's most populous northern metropolis and into Jigawa and Katsina, including major markets and textile clusters.

name: Port Harcourt Electricity Distribution Company (PHED)
summary: South-south DISCO for Rivers, Bayelsa, Cross River, and Akwa Ibom.
description: PHED operates from Port Harcourt, distributing power across the Niger Delta oil cities and the eastern coastal states, including major industrial and export facilities.

name: Yola Electricity Distribution Company (YEDC)
summary: Northeast DISCO for Adamawa, Taraba, Borno, and Yobe.
description: YEDC distributes grid power from Yola across the northeast savanna and Sahel fringe, including state capitals and agricultural towns in Adamawa, Taraba, Borno, and Yobe.
